text: Gamh was an Irish mythological site. The site lies in County Sligo. A holy well there was one of the Mirabilia Hiberniae, the wonders of Ireland. The well is half salt and half sweet. It rises from among three flagstones on the hill of Tullaghan. The well is now dedicated to St. Patrick. The story says it sprang up when the saint pursued a demon. The demon was called the Devil's Mother. Patrick grew thirsty and prayed for water, and the rock burst open. The demon came to drink, and her blood made the well bitter. The well keeps a pagan memory. It is said to shelter sacred salmon. Whoever catches one and eats it will see it frisking in the well the next day. The Dindshenchas, Ireland's place-poems, call the region Sliab Gamh. The name honors a servant of Eremon, the Milesian invader. Gamh was beheaded, perhaps for failing to observe agricultural rites. His head, thrown into the well, made its sweet water salty each day.

okr.objective: Record Gamh as the holy well in County Sligo and its mythological origin.
